newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee static on lack of dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee static on lack of dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee was static in early Wednesday trade, due to a lack of demand for dollars, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT the rupee was quoted at its opening level of 58.42 to the dollar. The currency closed at 58.43 on Tuesday.
"There is no commercial demand for dollars and with most banks either squared or carrying plus positions, the exchange rate is likely to stay at current levels," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank left the dollar-rupee exchange rate unchanged and buying and selling prices remained at 58.4026 and 59.5824.
"It is unlikely that banks are carrying minus dollar positions, since the downside which is close to the Central Bank's bottom is well cushioned," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were at 9.5 percent after opening at 10, with the market well offered, dealers said.
